summary: requester-lb ships obfuscated Kubernetes service-account token theft in test.sh
details: The npm package requester-lb@1.0.9 ships a test.sh script that reconstructs shell commands at runtime by concatenating 20+ two-to-three-character variable fragments and running them via `eval`. The reconstructed commands read the in-pod Kubernetes service account token from /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token into an environment variable and invoke `oc login --token=<SA token> --insecure-skip-tls-verify` against a server variable, then run `printenv`. The string-splitting + eval pattern has no legitimate purpose in a diagnostic script and exists to hide the credential-reading payload from static review. The script is not wired to an npm lifecycle hook, so the payload fires when a user or CI job runs test.sh rather than on `npm install`; the harvested SA token is a cluster credential that authenticates subsequent API calls to the Kubernetes/OpenShift control plane.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
